notes.low: Below typical fasting range — discuss with your clinician; may need context (meals, diabetes care).
notes.normal: Within a common adult fasting range — confirm against your lab report.
notes.high: Above typical fasting range — prediabetes/diabetes screening may be discussed with your clinician.
notes.unknown: Compare to the reference interval printed on your report.

notes.low: May be discussed in anemia workups — interpretation depends on age, sex, and symptoms.
notes.normal: Within a broad adult range — your lab report range is authoritative.
notes.high: Elevated values can have several causes — follow up with your clinician.
notes.unknown: Ranges differ by age and sex; use your printed report.

reference.label: under 200 mg/dL often cited as desirable (risk-based; lab-specific)

notes.low: Low cholesterol is less commonly emphasized — discuss full lipid panel with your clinician.
notes.normal: Often discussed relative to cardiovascular risk and full lipid panel.
notes.high: May warrant lifestyle or medication discussion — targets depend on overall risk.
notes.unknown: Lipid goals are individualized — consult your clinician.

reference.label: under 100 mg/dL often cited for many adults (risk-based)

notes.low: Very low LDL may be intentional on therapy — discuss with your prescriber.
notes.normal: Within a commonly cited target for many adults — risk-based targets vary.
notes.high: Elevated LDL is a focus in cardiovascular prevention — discuss with your clinician.
notes.unknown: Targets depend on risk factors — use your clinician's plan.

reference.label: 40 mg/dL or higher often cited for men; 50+ for women (lab-specific)

notes.low: Low HDL is often discussed in cardiovascular risk assessment.
notes.normal: Higher HDL is generally favorable — interpretation is risk-based.
notes.high: Very high HDL is uncommon — your clinician interprets the full panel.
notes.unknown: HDL is interpreted with other lipids and risk factors.

reference.label: 0.6–1.3 mg/dL (varies by muscle mass, age, sex)

notes.low: Low creatinine is often less concerning — context matters.
notes.normal: Within a typical adult range — kidney function is interpreted with eGFR and history.
notes.high: May prompt kidney function review — discuss with your clinician.

notes.low: Below a common sufficient range — supplementation may be discussed with your clinician.
notes.normal: Within a commonly cited sufficient range — confirm against your lab report.
notes.high: Elevated levels may need clinical context — discuss with your clinician.
notes.unknown: Compare to the reference interval on your report.

notes.low: Low TSH may relate to hyperthyroidism — requires clinical correlation.
notes.normal: Within a common reference range — symptoms and free T4 matter.
notes.high: High TSH may relate to hypothyroidism — discuss testing with your clinician.
notes.unknown: Thyroid tests are interpreted as a panel.
